studies.citation: Ahmad S et al. Gender-Specific Trends in Ophthalmologist Medicare Collections. Am J Ophthalmol. 2020;214:32–39.
studies.population: US ophthalmologists grouped by physician gender; sample size not verified
studies.payer: Medicare physician utilization and payment data
studies.finding: Women ophthalmologists collected 42% less after adjustment for age, geography and subspecialty. Women also saw fewer patients.
studies.limitation: Collections are not salary. Observational findings do not establish unequal rates for identical services or patient-sex discrimination.
studies.relevance: Context for clinician payment disparities; outside the primary patient-sex comparison.
studies.extraction_level: Abstract verified; full text not reviewed
studies.identity_reporting: Physician gender comparison; cisgender identity not verified. No patient-sex analysis.
studies.screening_notes: Not extracted: sample size, confidence interval and unadjusted totals.

studies.citation: Raber I et al. Gender Differences in Medicare Payments Among Cardiologists. JAMA Cardiol. 2021;6(12):1432–1439.
studies.finding: Median annual payments (men/women): inpatient $62,897/$45,288; outpatient $91,053/$51,975. Reported adjusted log coefficient for women: −0.06 (95% CI −0.11 to −0.02). No per-charge difference for the three most common billing codes in each setting.
studies.limitation: Work hours, encounter time and nonclinical duties unavailable; residual confounding. Payments are not salary. Findings do not compare patient sexes.
studies.relevance: Clinician-payment context; outside primary patient-sex synthesis.
studies.extraction_level: Targeted main-text review via indexed PMC; supplement not reviewed
studies.identity_reporting: Self-reported physician gender linked to NPI; cisgender identity not established.
studies.screening_notes: Adjusted for billing volume/diversity, case mix, experience and subspecialty. Formal risk-of-bias assessment pending.

provenance.source_access: Direct PMC page returned a browser challenge; indexed primary-source main text was accessible. Supplemental tables not independently reviewed.
